notes.title: Announcing: Electrosphere2d, Spheroid's Spiritual Successor
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone. It has been a while, and I- the developer of Spheroid- have some exciting news about Spheroid's future- but, more specifically, the future of its new spiritual successor, Electrosphere2d.

[url=https://gamejolt.com/games/electrosphere2d/514856][img]https://i.imgur.com/OPKGD2W.png[/img][/url]


According to the store page on Game Jolt:

in the 2D platforming spiritual successor to Fennecai Fox Creative's "Spheroid,"; you play as a robotic blue sphere equipped with a powerful electrical field, but no ability to jump. Collect data bytes, defeat patrolling enemies, and build up speed to roll through a variety of uniquely stylized environments at breakneck speeds! Journey to find out what happened to all the data that was recently stolen from the Blissful Hills datacenter!



Electrosphere2d is in a very much incomplete, pre-alpha status currently. The game is not ready to play, and development is now in the conceptual phase mostly.

I cannot announce a release date or open beta at this time, but I would like to announce this new game project for all of you who have supported Spheroid for this whole time.

The game will not release on steam.

If you would like to be notified about further development progress on Electrosphere2d and be notified when- and IF- it eventually releases on Game Jolt, you may click on the above image. The above image will take you to Gamejolt.com, where you can follow the game's development progress as soon as I have something worth sharing.

That's all I have to say for now; thank you for reading this surprising update- I look forward to hearing from you on the Game Jolt page soon!

notes.title: This Game Is Dead (not a prank, sorry)
notes.notes:
This is unironically not an April fools day joke.

I'm not going to go into detail. All I will say is that things didn't work out for Spheroid and I am deleting the store page soon, if not today.

If anyone who has bought the game in hopes of getting a future version for free is disappointed at all by this, please contact me as soon as possible: 1995aek@gmail.com

thank you. I will tie up loose ends (refunds, etc.) as necessary, requested, and possible.

notes.title: Potential Issues Due to steamworks fiddling
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, just a quick update:

You may experience issues launching the game due to recent fiddling with the steam-works settings on my end.

These settings have moved the game's files from "steamapps/Spheroid" into "steamapps/spheroid/Spheroid_public" and as such may cause the game to simply not launch.

To resolve this issue, please uninstall and then re-install the game via your steam library by right-clicking the game and choosing "uninstall", then installing as normal afterwords.

for the same reasons; I also have had to temporarily remove the "Classic" beta branch from spheroid.

For the time being, i am not planning on adding it back until the game's current major overhaul has been finished or close-to-finished, at which point i will add back the classic branch, and add the current version of the game to that branch. 

that said, it will have one less copyright-infringing song in it...you probably know the one. y'know, the one an entire level is based on. im working on that; but the old version of the project is going to be a painful mess to work with on my end if im not extremely careful, so the song isnt going to be removed from that until i know how to do so without crippling the entire unity project. If the song's copyright holders are reading this- thank you for your understanding.

notes.title: Current Status + VR possibility
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone. It has been a while sinc ei basically left everyone with the idea that "a big update is coming but the most recent one briefly failed and was rolled back."

So, its high time i let everyone know about Spheroid's current development status, and im going to be very honest about it.

At the moment, Spheroid is on hold for the forseeable future. When I first made this project, I was very passionate about it, but through massive technical hurdles having to be overcome constantly, I have burned myself out on this project. knowing of a sense of obligation to continue, yet also in spite of it to a degree, I may very well shelve this for a while to collect dust until a day when i feel like making something new with some of the idea's better parts. However, there is some good news in regaurds to this game:

Due to my recent purchase of the Oculus CV1 VR headset, there is now a very good chance that Spheroid will support VR in some form. Coupled with newfound techniques for creating my own art for the game, Spheroid can be expected to look way cooler and more consistent in potential future iterations or successors- In the meantime however, I would like to take a moment and thank my small playerbase for the support you have given me thus far. every bit counts, from the smallest comments to the longest critiques. 

For updates on other projects, and to just follow or hang out with me:

notes.title: A possible look at what's to come!

Hello everyone! Just a quick announcement:

I have decided to release my ideas as to what I would like to add to the game, in the form of a tentative road map of sorts.  You can see what features I want to add to the game, and my progress on them, here:

notes.title: Spheroid beta 12
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone! Today I have updated spheroid again. I haven't added any new content yet, and I apologize for that- but the 4th level is in the works, dont worry. :)

in the meantime, here's what has been changed or added:

* fixed being able to pause / interact with the main menu while there was a white fade happening (I think?)
* added an in-game pause menu link to the bug reporting / suggestions discussion
* redesigned the end of level 1. 
* added security cameras to the hub- [SYSTEM] is watching.
* made the ball able to roll slightly faster down ramps and along surfaces in anticipation of level 4.
* put the "laser core" spheroid unlock on a diet so it could fit on the level 2 elevator and look better.
* added more weird sci-fi sounds to level 1, and re-added the police siren sound that was apparently missing
* fixed a bug that made the lasers' sparking sound effect ignore the volume slider for sound effects
* added the ability to disable mouse locking from the main menu. this will probably be moved to the options menu in a future release.
* made some adjustments and fixes in level 3

notes.title: Spheroid beta 11: Biggest update yet! (also the first version on Steam)
notes.notes:
Hello! I have some exciting news (for anyone who originally got the game or saw the game on itch.io)

This is the BIGGEST update in spheroid yet! (not including updates before itch.io, the super early alpha, which i didnt ever keep track of)

Here are all the things I did in this update, in the order that I did them. Please note that changes lower in the list might in some cases be replacements of items higher in the list, or otherwise make higher items irrelevant or different. If your going to even bother reading this huge wall of text, I suggest you do so carefully. 

* added an icon

* changed company name to "Fennecai Fox Creative"

* added the ability to quit to the main menu alongside the button that quits the game

* fixed an issue where the lights on the ball were still super bright on most levels when starting as the default spheroid

* fixed a game-breaking issue where the very first door wouldn't open, prohibiting any progress whatsoever....I think...

* adjusted the opening cut scene voice-acting

* made the loading screen tips text bigger

* removed a sound from the soundscape of level 1

* Switched the font of the menus to match the new spheroid logo, accept 
where it would possibly be less legible than the original font.

* replaced the "Spheroid (beta)" text with a new logo on the main menu (but still made it clear this is a beta)

* improved the main menu scenery

* made some more changes to the hub's art

* adjusted the intro cut scene a little bit

* changed the sound the menu buttons make

* made subtle lighting changes so that the build didn't take the next century

* fixed an issue where the tubes in the background of level 3 were all white 
(I'm honestly not sure if this happened in the previous beta 10 build, but its fixed now either way.)

* heavily optimized the "level pipe" particle effect...hopefully.

* upgraded literally everything to the Unity 2018 beta render pipeline, only to realize it screwed everything up and reverted to a very fortunate recent backup of the project i had laying around. no changes have been lost.

* level 2 now looks like plywood rather than bamboo, the way I originally intended.

* removed a piece of wood from level 2 that said "brakedown" on it due to concern that the meme this level was inspired by is too old now for anyone to know what part of it that actually was

* replaced and upgraded a few models and a lot of materials

* made changes to level 1's scenery as a result of the material upgrades

* finally actually tested the game and realized a bunch of serious issues, which i fixed

* added the steamworks api/sdk/whatever into the project's files for future use

* fixed an issue in level 1 where some hint text said "SPACE is the spacebar" or "E is the spacebar" or whatever, depending on what you had configured as your USE key.

* moved the button that quits to the hub into the "Quit" menu in the pause menu.

* fixed a potential issue with the "Vocal" audio volume slider

* adjusted the intro cut scene's voice-acting performance/sound effects

* made some more small changes to the hub's art

* baked occlusion culling for all 3 currently existing levels- this should speed things up pretty well! if not, let me know asap!

* fixed pixelation on text in some places

* fixed bad lighting in one spot of level 1

* made a hint easier to read in level 1

* heavily updated the checkpoints- you should now be able to resume a level where you left off, provided it is the most recently played level.

* completely overhauled the save system in the process - Old save data will not be loaded into the new system. sorry, itch.io version players!

* added visual grain to level 3

* removed an incredibly powerful cheat code (for technical reasons. i might re-add it later!)

* fixed a couple of terrible camera angles in level 3

* tweaked and changed the intro cutscene to "near" perfection (some stuff still NYI)

* fixed issues with the intro cutscene

* broke a huge amount of things by refactoring my code for the first time, which may or may not have negated some of the above to a degree

* re-fixed or just plain fixed all of those broken things

* added particle effects to activatable vacuum tubes and wooden doors

* lost track of what else
